Welcome
Welcome to Wandsworth Preparatory School! We are a close knit community driven by a shared vision and unwavering commitment to excellence. Our small school is nestled near the edge of Wandsworth Common and the children benefit greatly from the beautiful natural environment surrounding our school.
At Wandsworth Preparatory, our vision is clear: we aspire for our pupils to be confident individuals with a real passion for learning. We champion academic success alongside the development of character, fostering a deep-rooted respect and empathy for others. Pupils at our school are happy to take risks, try new things and hone their skills and talents.

📚 Buddy reading Our Reception children welcomed Year 2 children to their class for a special reading session. The Year 2 joined the Reception class to listen to them read, helping with tricky words, sounding out and talking about the stories together.Buddy reading is a wonderful way for older and younger children to learn from one another. It’s also a lovely way to build friendships across the year groups.Looking forward to the next session already! 📕 🏫 If you’d like to see our children in action and find out what makes our school so special and unique get in touch to arrange a tour.#readingisfun #wandsworthmums #claphammums #learningtogether #readingforpleasure
A snapshot 📸 of our week 🐅 The tiger really did come to tea in Pre Prep Nursery to support their book of the week🌳 Forest school for lower school at Wimbledon Common🔠 Phonics in Reception ⚖️ Measuring and weighing in Reception🐝 Sharing home learning to the class in Year 2✏️ Working on different story openings to capture a reader’s attention from the first sentence in Year 6And to add to all that we celebrated national poetry day with our whole school poetry cafe - more on that next week! Have a wonderful restful weekend!#claphammums #prepschoollife #insidetheclassroom #learningforlife #wandsworthmums

🌳 Forest school is a much loved part of life at Wandsworth Prep. Last week our new Reception and Pre Prep Nursery children experienced it for the first time, it was a wonderful way to end the first full week! ☀️ 🌧️ Come rain or shine, our amazing forest school lead Ms Sokoli guides the children through hands on, experiential leading to build confidence, resilience, teamwork and a willingness to take risks.Activities are carefully linked to seasonal changes and follow our curriculum, giving children the opportunity to explore, discover and connect with nature in a meaningful way 🌱 ✨ Learning beyond the classroom at its very best the WPS way 💙 #outdoorlearning #forestschool #wimbledoncommon #learningoutsidetheclassroom #claphamlondon
🧗 🏫 While the children were enjoying their summer holidays, we were busy making some exciting improvements to our playground! We’ve added new sports Astro, a traversing climbing frame (kindly funded by our PTA) and reduced and updated the decking to create more space to play!It’s been fantastic to see the children enjoying their new look playground over the past two weeks, climbing, running, playing and making the most of their bigger and brighter space 🏃‍♂️ ☀️ If you’d like to see the school for yourself, get in touch with admissions@wandsworthprep.com to arrange a tour! #wandsworthmums #wandsworthcommon #claphammums #outdoorlearning #schoolupdate
As part of this term’s project, Year 1 and Year 2 visited the Wetlands Centre @wwtlondon this week for a wonderfully immersive day of learning.The children took part in an engaging workshop all about minibeasts, working collaboratively to sort them based on their features before heading outdoors to search for their own! 🔎 They discovered worms, spiders, ladybird larvae, snails, grasshoppers and woodlice, before taking the time to carefully observe and sketch what they had found ✏️ 🐌 Despite the rain, the children had a fantastic time getting hands on with their learning. A wonderful opportunity to explore, investigate and discover beyond the classroom 🌳 #handsonlearningfun #schooltrip #claphammums #wandsworthmums #learningthroughnature
We are delighted to announce the appointment of Mrs Joanna Desforges as Head of Wandsworth Prep from January 2027.Jo joins us from Hurlingham School in Putney, where she is currently Deputy Head, Teaching, Learning and Innovation. She brings more than 15 years of experience in education, with a career spanning independent co-educational prep schools.Jo’s journey into education began when she retrained as a teacher after her own children started school. Her passion is putting each individual child at the heart of their education and ensuring that every child has the opportunity to learn, grow and thrive.Speaking about her appointment, Jo said:“For me, it is about being part of a community with a shared purpose and values; getting to know every child and having fun while exploring learning in a creative and dynamic environment. Wandsworth Prep already has strong foundations, with high-quality teaching and learning at its heart, and I’m excited by the opportunity to build on these — embracing innovation and continuing to develop a warm, welcoming and truly unique school community.”We look forward to welcoming Jo to the school community in January! ✨💙
And just like that……we’re back 📚 ✨ It’s been wonderful to see all the children back at school and seeing the new pupils settling in so well! We’re already back to learning, discovering, creating and of course, having fun with friends! Here’s a quick snap shot of what was happening in the classrooms yesterday:🎶 Music, maths and play in Pre Prep Nursery and Reception✏️ 1-1 reading in Year 2🏃‍♀️ PE in Year 1🎨 Art in Year 5🌍 Geography in Year 3Here’s to a year full of learning, new experiences and lots of wonderful memories! 💙 #wandsworthmums #claphammums #prepschools #londonschool #learningandgrowing

Our Ethos and Values
Our Ethos and Values
At Wandsworth Preparatory School, we are guided by the belief that a happy child is a learning child. Through a culture that nurtures our school values of curiosity, compassion, courage, collaboration and creativity, we strive to ensure that every child feels valued, supported and inspired to achieve their full potential. We want our pupils to leave Wandsworth Prep as happy, confident and compassionate individuals, equipped with the knowledge, skills and character to become curious lifelong learners, ready to embrace challenges, think independently and contribute positively to an ever-changing world.
Our values are at the heart of everything we do. They provide a shared language to help develop the character, attitudes and habits that will support children throughout their time with us and beyond.
Developed in partnership with our school community and informed by research from the Jubilee Centre for Character and Virtues, our values reflect the four pillars of character development: moral, civic, intellectual and performance.
Curiosity
Curiosity is the desire to know more and to understand the world around us. Children express curiosity by asking questions, seeking answers and exploring ideas beyond what they already know. At Wandsworth Prep School, we actively foster curiosity, as it plays a vital role in developing critical thinking skills, encouraging independence, and nurturing a lifelong love of learning.
Collaboration
Collaboration is working together which could be towards achieving a shared goal or through collaboration with a peer to support their learning journey. At Wandsworth Prep School, we value the importance of teamwork and provide opportunities for children to develop the skills needed to collaborate effectively. Children learn to work respectfully towards a shared goal by listening to others and sharing ideas.
Compassion
Compassion is showing care, concern and empathy towards others. At Wandsworth Prep School, we value the importance of understanding and care for those around us, including our wider community. We encourage our learners to recognise their own feelings as well as the feelings and experiences of others, ensuring that everyone, including ourselves, is treated with kindness and respect.
Courage
Courage is the ability to face challenges with confidence and determination. At Wandsworth Prep School, we value resilience and foster a positive growth mindset that encourages children to embrace new opportunities and ‘have a go’. Courage means stepping outside our comfort zones, asking for help when needed, listening to feedback, and viewing mistakes as valuable opportunities for learning and growth.
Creativity
Creativity is the ability to use imagination and original ideas to create something new. At Wandsworth Prep, we encourage our learners to explore ideas in different ways, think outside the box and develop the confidence to express themselves. Through creative learning, pupils build independence, perseverance and an understanding of how to adapt and refine their ideas as they grow.
We dream big, we work hard, we achieve the extraordinary.
I really value the education and experience the school is providing my child.

About Us
Welcome to Wandsworth Prep School
Welcome to Wandsworth Preparatory School! We are a close knit community driven by a shared vision and unwavering commitment to excellence. Our small school, for boys and girls ages 3-11, is nestled near the edge of Wandsworth Common and the children benefit greatly from the beautiful natural environment surrounding our school.
At Wandsworth Preparatory, our vision is clear: we aspire for our pupils to be confident individuals with a real passion for learning. We champion academic success alongside the development of character, fostering a deep-rooted respect and empathy for others. Pupils at our school are happy to take risks, try new things and hone their skills and talents.
Our mission is simple yet profound: to cultivate an environment where academic rigour meets creative expression, empowering our students to thrive. We believe in the power of immersive, interconnected learning experiences tailored to each child’s unique interests and needs.
At the heart of our core values lies a dedication to understanding and celebrating the individuality of every student. We recognise that true excellence stems from embracing diversity and nurturing each child’s distinct talents.
Join us at Wandsworth Preparatory School, where we not only educate minds but also nurture hearts and character. Together, let’s embark on a journey of discovery, growth, and endless possibilities.

Growth Mindset
At Wandsworth Prep, we want every pupil to be a successful learner. Most importantly, we recognise that instilling positive attitudes towards learning will ensure pupils progress and reach their potential. Consequently, a critical concept shaping our school’s ethos is Growth Mindset, based on the work of Carol Dweck.
As a Growth Mindset school, we actively encourage challenge, resilience, and effort in all pupils. We believe everyone’s abilities and talents are developed through dedication and hard work. Our pupils are urged to view mistakes as an essential part of learning.
The results below are from our Pupil Surveys and are a testament to our excellent teaching practices and Growth Mindset culture.

Pupil Voice
At Wandsworth Prep, we understand the importance of Pupil Voice and feel they have the opportunity to voice their opinions and be listened to when shaping the future of their school, community and broader world.
Providing children with skills in leadership, empathy and decision making, our main aim is to create a positive and inclusive community within the school which prepares children for the responsibilities, opportunities and experiences of life.
The School Council is a student body of two children from every year group whom their peers nominate. Our School Council meets once a week with the School Council Lead to aid in facilitating the meetings. The children work together to create action plans, delegate jobs, run whole school assemblies and hold meetings to get their project up and running!
To see more about our School Council, click here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wandsworth Preparatory School | School Council | Senior School London | Wandsworth Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
School Council
Our School Council is a student body of two children from every year group, who their fellow peers nominate. The nominees work on preparing a speech to persuade their peers as to why they are fit for the role, and a vote is then taken, falling in line with our British Values and creating a democratic ethos.
The School Council meets once a week. Using ideas from the rest of the school, they pick one project each term to work on, focusing on either an improvement or enrichment project for the school, local community or an environmental project. The children work together to create action plans, delegate jobs, run whole school assemblies and hold meetings to get their project up and running!
A few examples of our past projects featured within our latest news are the Wandsworth Prep Recycling Project’ where we worked with the local council to evaluate our rubbish and recycling, ‘Switch Off Fortnight’ in collaboration with EDF Energy, focused on saving energy, working with Wandsworth Age UK making Christmas cards and singing carols at Gwynneth Morgan day centre and WPS Walk to School Week. The whole school’s collaboration with these projects gives every child an equal opportunity to get involved and creates an inclusive and nurturing school community.

Curriculum
The Wandsworth Preparatory School curriculum has been carefully designed to ensure each child can fulfil their potential, tailored to their needs and future aspirations. Our curriculum is challenging, engaging and diverse, considering the National Curriculum’s expectations.
We aim to create a learning environment where children are not only prepared for examination success but also develop a life-long love of learning. Children who can work and think independently, are motivated, creative and confident with the skills to solve problems, collaborate and communicate effectively will be best placed to succeed at senior schools and in life itself; these are the qualities we seek to encourage and develop.
Learn how we prepare our students for the 11+ here.
Subjects
English
English at Wandsworth Prep is for our pupils to develop a love of reading and writing.
To develop a love of reading, all children need access to high-quality text; therefore, our rigorous programme of daily phonics from Reception to Year 2 ensures decoding and fluency. Our daily Shared Reading in Lower School and Guided Reading sessions from Year 2 to Year 6 offer a wonderfully warm environment to discuss and analyse texts.
Spelling is taught through a comprehensive spelling programme which runs throughout the school, and we strongly believe in embedding these spelling strategies as part of our daily writing. Writing should be a stimulating experience. We want our pupils to view themselves as authors from an early age, and we use our Growth Mindset learning environment to draft, share, edit and improve until we can publish and share our writing as authors throughout the school.
Technical accuracy is an integral part of our writing, and we embed this within our writing lessons in the same way sub-editors do when editing authors’ first drafts. All pupils have a wide variety of stimuli – from high-quality texts to the use of film and drama. Regular drama workshops in all classes enable pupils to enter the world of a story and bring depth and emotion to a pupil’s writing once they have experienced a dilemma in a workshop.
Find out more about Drama at Wandsworth Prep here.
Drama
Technical accuracy is an essential part of our writing, and we embed this within our writing lessons in the same way sub-editors do when editing authors’ first drafts. All pupils have a wide variety of stimuli – from high-quality texts to film and drama.
Regular drama workshops in all classes enable pupils to enter the world of a story and bring depth and emotion to a pupil’s writing once they have experienced a dilemma in a workshop. What could be more inspirational for writing a persuasive argument as Hermia in A Midsummer Night’s Dream than experiencing being a member of Duke Theseus’ courtroom? Only once the pupils have experienced being evacuated in World War II can they make sense of and compose a historical report fit for a non-fiction shelf.
Special events such as our end-of-term showcases highlight our innovative approach to drama and public speaking. All pupils are trained to present to adults at exhibitions to develop their public speaking skills and can do this confidently through ownership and a deep understanding of their writing pieces. Our now infamous annual Poetry Café delights our parent community every year, as do our annual Lower School Nativities (performed at Putney Arts Theatre) and our dramatic ensemble performances where every pupil has the opportunity to shine. View an example here.
“Pupils achieve excellent levels of attainment in all areas of literacy.” ISI Report, 2019
Maths
Maths at Wandsworth Prep is about creating independent, inquisitive and skilful mathematicians. We encourage a passion for this integral subject and equip pupils with the powerful toolset needed to understand and change the world. These tools include fluent and agile knowledge of numbers, logical reasoning, problem-solving skills and the ability to think abstractly.
At Wandsworth Preparatory School, we strongly feel about developing pupils’ mental and lateral thinking skills and consider the proper communication of Maths as paramount in pupils’ understanding. After all, it is like another language in many respects. From the earliest ages, we drive the pupils to extend their thinking.
Through hands-on and practical activities, pupils in Early Years and Key Stage 1 have almost constant exposure to appropriate real-life material and resources. Across the school, a strong emphasis is placed on the process rather than simply the outcome, and we strive to make Maths enthralling for all our young learners and ensure a sense of achievement is experienced.
Interest and motivation in Maths are promoted through a dedicated Maths Week in the spring term, placing a schoolwide emphasis on enjoyment in Maths and the importance of problem-solving, strategy and lateral thinking skills. School subscriptions to both the Manga High and MyMaths websites and regular iPad use in lessons also boost enthusiasm for the subject across the school.
Project
Project learning at Wandsworth Prep comprises History, Geography, Art, Design Technology, Religious Studies and computing, and strives to engender a thirst for knowledge of the world, be it physical, historical or spiritual. Underpinning this aim is the belief that project teaching and learning should be an enjoyable, creative and magical experience for pupils and teachers alike. It can significantly contribute to children’s physical, intellectual, social and emotional development.
Rather than being taught each foundation subject discretely, the children follow a new learning journey every term, which includes fictional adventures and skills-based challenges. Each Project commences with a ‘hook’ that captures the pupils’ attention and sparks intrigue, such as the classroom being transformed into an art gallery.
Every project incorporates the National Curriculum objectives in a creative way that provides the children with a context for their learning, engaging them fully and actively in the learning process. Pupils receive academic rigour whilst understanding how these subjects link with one another and beyond. At the end of each term, we provide opportunities to showcase the learning from our projects so that the children can share their knowledge with family and friends.
Science
Science at Wandsworth Prep aims to cultivate a natural curiosity for the world around us. Through Science, the children are allowed to develop vital skills to begin to make sense of scientific matters they come across in the news and their everyday lives.
The Science curriculum is covered practically through investigations in collaboration with building up in-depth subject knowledge. They work on building up their skills in observation, questioning, analysis, data handling, and writing predictions and conclusions.
Excitement and natural curiosity towards Science are developed through a whole school Science Week that happens once a year which includes a variety of workshops, external speakers, parent speakers and investigations that are child-led and then presented by the children in a Science Fair to the rest of the school.
We aim for the children to leave Wandsworth Prep equipped with the necessary skills and curiosity to want to further their Science education as they graduate from their secondary schools and beyond.
Forest school
Forest School at Wandsworth Prep offers a place where children can experience activities in an outdoor environment as a regular part of their school life. We bring learning to life through various stimulating experiences that encourage team building, making choices and taking risks, all in a safe and friendly environment.
Wandsworth Prep ​Forest School is delivered in an area of Wimbledon Common and Putney Heath forest, where we offer exciting and fun outdoor activities for all pupils across the school.
Forest School is designed to promote the holistic development of children using a child-centred approach. Our Forest School experience provides children with opportunities to achieve and develop confidence through hands-on learning within the outdoor environment. The impact of which; raises aspirations, a sense of achievement and self-esteem. We are widening the horizons of all participating and leaving a lasting impression. In addition, the children learn to take risks safely by learning to assess the risks of activities independently.
Sport
At Wandsworth Prep, all year groups are taught by a specialist PE teacher. In the Early Years Foundation Stage, Years 1 and 2, children are taught to be active and interactive and to develop their coordination, control, and movement. We provide opportunities for children to become physically confident in a way which supports a healthy and active lifestyle. Within lessons, children work as individuals, in a group or as part of a team. Children develop core movement, become increasingly competent and confident and access a broad range of opportunities to extend their agility, balance and coordination.
Reception and Year 1 pupils are taught P.E on site, and Year 2 learn at Wandsworth Common. Reception and Year 1 attend swimming lessons in the summer term to kickstart their love of swimming and to begin those swimming foundations.
In Years 3 – 6, children can polish their skills with a focus on fewer sports to improve the quality and standard of their play. P.E lessons are taught at The Wandle Recreation Centre, where we train on the Astro pitches and Sports hall. In the Autumn term, we teach football and netball, hockey in the Spring term and athletics and cricket in the summer term. Fixtures against other schools occur during games afternoons and offer competitive opportunities for children of all abilities, as does our inclusive summer Sports Day and charity runs or exercise events.
We also support those exhibiting strong sporting talent, allowing them to represent the school in the Independent Schools Association tournaments, competing at the highest levels.
The curriculum is also enriched by after-school clubs, such as Gymnastics and Tag Rugby. Dance and ballet are also offered, where children can gain certificates awarded by the Royal Academy of Dance.
Music
At Wandsworth Prep, we want to ensure that each child can enjoy and appreciate music. From Reception to Year 6, all our children benefit from music lessons taught by a specialist music teacher.
Children follow a programme based on the fundamental activities of:
Music Express underpins teaching and learning. Music Express provides a carefully-structured progressive scheme of work for music, integrating singing, playing, listening and composing. Planning also enables a cross-curricular, topic-based approach to music so that learning about music is developed whilst exploring different topics and is linked with other curriculum subjects.
Children prepare a range of songs for key events such as drama productions, the Christmas Concert, the Easter Assembly and the Summer concert. Workshops and visits allow pupils to work with outside professionals.
Children can learn an instrument individually, such as the violin, piano or guitar. They can perform in informal and formal concerts or assemblies throughout the year and take exams set by Trinity College of Music, where appropriate.
Creativity
Creativity is about inspiring through memorable learning experiences and can be a platform for the establishment of personalised learning, enabling children to think for themselves and branch out into areas of curiosity and interest. We can move away from teaching discrete, isolated subjects and develop more innovative and practical approaches to teaching to create a curriculum tailored to children’s specific needs and interests.
Each term, a project is planned based on a science, geography or history focus that teaches children the fundamental skills to learn across various topics. When planning a project, our enquiry-led approach to learning requires the teachers to have the end ‘goal’ in sight concerning learning outcomes. Our approach ensures that our children are excited about learning, feel involved in the process and anticipate what will happen next.
Performing Arts
At Wandsworth Preparatory School, the performing arts curriculum is designed to provide students with a wide range of opportunities to explore, create, and perform music, drama, and dance. The curriculum is structured around four key areas: music, drama, dance, and cross-curricular projects.
In the music area of the curriculum, students are introduced to a variety of musical concepts and skills, including pitch, rhythm, melody, and form. They are also given the opportunity to sing, play instruments, and compose their own music. Students may have the opportunity to participate in choir, instrumental ensembles, and individual music lessons.
In the drama area of the curriculum, students are encouraged to use their imaginations and develop their creativity through role-play, improvisation, and scripted performances. They are also given the opportunity to learn about different aspects of theatre, such as stagecraft, character development, and scriptwriting.
In the dance area of the curriculum, students are introduced to different styles of dance and movement, including ballet, jazz, and contemporary dance. They are also given the opportunity to create their own dance routines and perform them for their peers and the wider school community.
In addition to these dedicated music, drama, and dance areas of the curriculum, students at Wandsworth Preparatory School may also have the opportunity to participate in cross-curricular projects that bring together elements of the performing arts with other subject areas. For example, students may work on a project that involves creating a musical based on a science theme, or creating a dance piece inspired by a historical event.

Curriculum
The Wandsworth Preparatory School curriculum has been carefully designed to ensure each child can fulfil their potential, tailored to their needs and future aspirations. Our curriculum is challenging, engaging and diverse, considering the National Curriculum’s expectations.
We aim to create a learning environment where children are not only prepared for examination success but also develop a life-long love of learning. Children who can work and think independently, are motivated, creative and confident with the skills to solve problems, collaborate and communicate effectively will be best placed to succeed at senior schools and in life itself; these are the qualities we seek to encourage and develop.
Learn how we prepare our students for the 11+ here.
Subjects
English
English at Wandsworth Prep is for our pupils to develop a love of reading and writing.
To develop a love of reading, all children need access to high-quality text; therefore, our rigorous programme of daily phonics from Reception to Year 2 ensures decoding and fluency. Our daily Shared Reading in Lower School and Guided Reading sessions from Year 2 to Year 6 offer a wonderfully warm environment to discuss and analyse texts.
Spelling is taught through a comprehensive spelling programme which runs throughout the school, and we strongly believe in embedding these spelling strategies as part of our daily writing. Writing should be a stimulating experience. We want our pupils to view themselves as authors from an early age, and we use our Growth Mindset learning environment to draft, share, edit and improve until we can publish and share our writing as authors throughout the school.
Technical accuracy is an integral part of our writing, and we embed this within our writing lessons in the same way sub-editors do when editing authors’ first drafts. All pupils have a wide variety of stimuli – from high-quality texts to the use of film and drama. Regular drama workshops in all classes enable pupils to enter the world of a story and bring depth and emotion to a pupil’s writing once they have experienced a dilemma in a workshop.
Find out more about Drama at Wandsworth Prep here.
Drama

Regular drama workshops in all classes enable pupils to enter the world of a story and bring depth and emotion to a pupil’s writing once they have experienced a dilemma in a workshop. What could be more inspirational for writing a persuasive argument as Hermia in A Midsummer Night’s Dream than experiencing being a member of Duke Theseus’ courtroom? Only once the pupils have experienced being evacuated in World War II can they make sense of and compose a historical report fit for a non-fiction shelf.
Special events such as our end-of-term showcases highlight our innovative approach to drama and public speaking. All pupils are trained to present to adults at exhibitions to develop their public speaking skills and can do this confidently through ownership and a deep understanding of their writing pieces. Our now infamous annual Poetry Café delights our parent community every year, as do our annual Lower School Nativities (performed at Putney Arts Theatre) and our dramatic ensemble performances where every pupil has the opportunity to shine. View an example here.

pageCache.text:
Early Years Curriculum
At Wandsworth Preparatory School, practitioners use the principles of the Early Years Foundation Stage framework, published on the 27th of March 2012, to guide everyday teaching and learning.
The Early Learning goals
The Early Learning goals set out what most children are expected to achieve by the end of the Foundation Stage. They are organised into seven areas of learning:
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Physical Development
Communication and Language
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World
Expressive Arts and Design
Subjects
English
At Wandsworth Preparatory School, English is designed to give students a strong foundation in language and literacy skills. The curriculum is structured around six areas of learning: communication and language; physical development; personal, social and emotional development; literacy; mathematics; and understanding the world.
Students are taught to listen and respond to others, speak clearly and confidently, and understand and follow instructions. They are also introduced to new vocabulary and concepts through stories, rhymes, and songs.
Pupils are taught the foundations of reading and writing, including letter recognition, phonics, and basic sight words. They are also encouraged to express themselves creatively through writing, drawing, and other forms of self-expression.
English curriculum at Wandsworth Preparatory School is designed to be inclusive, engaging, and developmentally appropriate for young children. It is structured to provide students with a strong foundation in language and literacy skills, and to encourage them to be curious, creative, and confident learners.
Maths
At Wandsworth Preparatory School, students are introduced to basic concepts such as counting, shape, and measurement. They are also encouraged to develop their problem-solving and reasoning skills through hands-on activities and games.
Some specific math skills that students may learn in Reception include:
In addition to learning math concepts and skills, students at Wandsworth Preparatory School are also encouraged to develop positive attitudes towards math. This includes developing confidence in their own ability to do math, as well as developing an interest in and enjoyment of math activities.
To support students in their math learning, teachers at Wandsworth Preparatory School use a variety of teaching methods, including whole-class instruction, small-group work, and individual activities. They also use a variety of materials and manipulatives, such as number lines, counting bears, and geoboards, to help students understand and apply mathematical concepts.
Counting objects and identifying numerals
Comparing and ordering numbers
Adding and subtracting small numbers

pageCache.text:
Extra Curricular Clubs
Wandsworth Prep offers an impressive and exciting array of extracurricular clubs designed to enrich the taught curriculum. We encourage pupils from Prep Prep to Year 6 to partake in various activities, helping develop and nurture every child’s strengths and interests.
We want to expand children’s knowledge and skills beyond the classroom, allowing them to develop their understanding and confidence.
Each term, we provide a diverse range of clubs, which we add to regularly to meet the needs of the children, ensuring plenty of fun and enriching activities for all pupils.
Our extra-curricular clubs take place after school until 5:00pm when children are collected by parents or go on to Wrap Around.
In addition to our engaging club list, Wandsworth Prep School offers comprehensive wraparound care to support busy families. From the end of the school day until 6 pm, care is provided included in the fees.
We also offer a breakfast club starting at 7:30 am. Children can enjoy a freshly prepared breakfast from our made-to-order menu for just £2.50, or attend the club without breakfast at no extra cost.
Every child is guaranteed a space at wraparound.

Open Days
We would love to have you visit us at Wandsworth Prep. We hold small group tours and private tours with our Head and team.
Small Group Tours are one of the best ways to help influence your decision for your child’s educational provision. At Wandsworth Prep, we arrange tours to give you the opportunity to take a tour of the school to see it in action, meet with teachers, support staff and the Head, and talk with the children of WPS to see why they love our school so much.
Small Group Tour – Thursday 24th September 9am: SOLD OUT
Open Week – Monday 5th- Friday 9th: email admissions@wandsworthprep.com to book a slot
Simply fill out the form below to register your interest. If you can’t make the dates please let us know in the form and we’ll be in touch with further dates.
During your visit to our school, you will have the opportunity to see the school in action through a tour, meeting our teachers, support staff, and senior leadership team.
